idiom_name: XCTestCase subclass conforms to the collaborator protocol and passes self
implementation_notes: XCTestCase is a class, so a test case can declare conformance to the collaborator protocol directly and pass self into the SUT, recording in instance properties; XCTest creates a fresh instance per test method, which keeps the recording per-test. For a closure-typed seam, a small reference box (or a captured local) holds the recorded values instead, and Swift Testing's struct-based suites force that box because a struct test instance cannot be mutated through a callback. Conformance stays justified when the protocol has several members or the test case is already the natural fixture; a hand-written conforming class or the local box is the norm, and mock libraries are not required.
pitfalls: An escaping closure that captures self strongly, held by a SUT the test also owns, forms a retain cycle; capture a recording box or use [weak self].
Conforming to an @objc or Sendable protocol can add requirements (NSObject inheritance, actor isolation) that change how the test case runs; check the protocol's constraints before shunting it.
Swift Testing suites are structs, so the callback cannot mutate the suite in place -- recording must go through a reference box or an actor.
